title: JavaScript — Objects, references, mutation, and copying

questions.question: let object1 = {value:10}; let object2 = object1; let object3 = {value:10}; object1 == object3 is:
options: false, because they are different objects.
true, because the fields are equal.
true, because == compares fields for objects.
false, because object3 used const.
questions.explanation: == / === on objects test identity. Same fields do not make one object.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: When we have two numbers, 120 and 120, we can consider them precisely the same number, whether or not they refer to the same physical bits.

questions.question: object1.value = 15 after object2 = object1. object2.value is:
options: 10, because assignment copied the fields.
15, because both names grasp the same object.
undefined, because value was replaced on object1 only.
15 on object1 and 10 on object2.
questions.explanation: Mutation is visible through every alias.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: The object1 and object2 bindings grasp the same object, which is why changing object1 also changes the value of object2.

questions.question: const task = { status: "open" }; task.status = "done". Does that throw?
options: Yes; const freezes the object.
Yes in strict mode only.
No; const blocks rebinding task, not field writes.
No, but status stays "open" because strings are const.
questions.explanation: task = {} would throw. task.status = "done" is allowed.

reference.book: JavaScript: The Definitive Guide, 7th Edition by David Flanagan
reference.excerpt: Objects are different than primitives. First, they are mutable—their values can change.

questions.question: const copy = { ...task }; copy.tags.push("late") when tags is nested. What happens to task.tags?
options: Unchanged; spread deep-clones arrays.
The push throws because copy is frozen.
tags becomes undefined on task.
It also gains "late" because the array is shared.
questions.explanation: Shallow copy. Nested arrays stay aliased.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Objects work differently. You can change their properties, causing a single object value to have different content at different times.

questions.question: updateTask should leave unmatched tasks as the same references. Why?
options: So React-style identity checks and tests can see what actually changed.
Because JavaScript forbids copying objects.
So JSON.stringify ignores them.
Because map cannot return new objects.
questions.explanation: Return task unchanged when id does not match. Spread a new object only for the match.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: They are said to have the same identity.

questions.question: Find the bug: function setStatus(tasks, id, status) { const t = tasks.find(x => x.id === id); t.status = status; return tasks; }
options: find cannot locate numbers.
It mutates the caller’s objects in place.
return tasks is illegal after find.
status must be written with Object.freeze.
questions.explanation: If the API is immutable, map to a new array instead of assigning t.status.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: The object1 and object2 bindings grasp the same object

questions.question: row.customer?.name when customer is null:
options: throws TypeError.
is null.name as a string.
is undefined.
creates a customer object.
questions.explanation: Optional chaining short-circuits to undefined. It does not invent data.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Objects allow us to group values—including other objects—to build more complex structures.

questions.question: Two appointments share one customer object. Renaming through appointment B:
options: leaves A’s customer name unchanged.
copies the customer automatically on write.
throws, because objects cannot be shared.
changes A as well, because the nested object is aliased.
questions.explanation: Give each appointment its own nested copy if they must diverge.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: The binding object3 points to a different object, which initially contains the same properties as object1 but lives a separate life.

questions.question: C++ struct passed by value copies fields. JS function (task) { task.status = "done" }:
options: receives a reference; the caller’s object mutates.
copies the struct; the caller is unchanged.
freezes task because parameters are const.
passes a pointer you must delete.
questions.explanation: The local binding task grasps the same object the caller passed.

reference.book: JavaScript: The Definitive Guide, 7th Edition by David Flanagan
reference.excerpt: Objects are different than primitives. First, they are mutable—their values can change.

questions.question: const t = {id:1,status:"open"}; const u = {...t, status:"done"}; t === u is:
options: true, because id is the same.
false, because spread made a new object.
true in strict mode only.
false because status is a string.
questions.explanation: t.status stays "open". u is a different object.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: With objects, there is a difference between having two references to the same object and having two different objects that contain the same properties.

questions.question: Numbers and strings are immutable. Objects are not. Which assignment mutates?
options: s[0] = "X" on a string s, which updates the literal.
n++ on a number binding, which changes that number value in the heap.
task.status = "done" on an object.
const n = 1, which freezes the integer 1 globally.
questions.explanation: Rebinding a number is not mutating the number 1. Object fields change in place.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: The types of values discussed in earlier chapters, such as numbers, strings, and Booleans, are all immutable

questions.question: Which copy is shallow?
options: { ...task }
Object.assign({}, task)
structuredClone(task) for a JSON-like task
const copy = task
questions.explanation: Spread and Object.assign copy one level. const copy = task is an alias, not a copy. structuredClone is deep for many values.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: You can change their properties, causing a single object value to have different content at different times.

questions.question: for...in on a task object without Object.hasOwn can pick up:
options: only own fields, always.
array indexes even when it is not an array.
symbol keys only.
inherited enumerable keys from the prototype.
questions.explanation: Prefer Object.keys or Object.entries, or hasOwn inside for...in.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Objects allow us to group values—including other objects—to build more complex structures.

questions.question: renameCustomer should not mutate the input appointment. Which return value is right?
options: A new appointment whose customer is also a new object.
The same appt after appt.customer.name = name.
A new appointment that still shares customer by reference.
undefined after deleting appt.customer.
questions.explanation: { ...appt, customer: { ...appt.customer, name } } copies both levels you change.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: The binding object3 points to a different object

questions.question: task.assignee when the field was never set is:
options: null
undefined
a ReferenceError
questions.explanation: Missing properties are undefined, not a throw (unless you opted into extra strict tools).

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: Objects allow us to group values—including other objects—to build more complex structures.

questions.question: Write withStatus(task, status): new object, other fields copied shallowly.
questions.explanation: Do not assign task.status. Return a new object.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: With objects, there is a difference between having two references to the same object and having two different objects that contain the same properties.

questions.question: Write updateTask(tasks, id, patch): new array; unmatched tasks keep identity.
hints: map. If task.id !== id return task. Else { ...task, ...patch }.
questions.explanation: Unmatched elements must be the same reference, not a spread copy.

reference.book: Eloquent JavaScript, 4th Edition by Marijn Haverbeke
reference.excerpt: They are said to have the same identity.

questions.question: Write renameCustomer(appt, name): new appointment and new customer; do not mutate input.
hints: Copy appt and copy customer in the same expression.
questions.explanation: One spread is not enough; the nested customer would still be shared.
